executive_summary: USD/JPY closed at 157.87 on 2026-10-02 in the gated price store, one session after the valuation date. The quote is yen per dollar, so a rising pair means a stronger dollar. Spot sits at the 56th percentile of its 52-week closing range (150.32–163.87). The pair is +1.32% over one month, −2.62% over three months, −0.71% over six months and +4.38% over one year. The core story is two central banks hiking at once. The Fed went to 3.75–4.00% by a 12-0 vote and the BoJ to 1.25% by 7-2. That leaves a +262.5bp policy gap that helps the pair on level but hurts it on trajectory, and September showed the level is not transmitting: the 10-year spread widened about 39bp while the pair fell to 152.91 on 2026-09-08 before rebounding. Taken alone, the dossiers would put the pair firmly higher over four weeks: USD tactical +0.3782 against JPY −0.028, a +0.406 spread. Two pair-specific features cut the scored tactical reading to +0.1265. The first is the joint US-Japan intervention put, which caps the topside. The second is the calendar: the BoJ's Outlook Report on 2026-10-30 lands 48 hours after the FOMC. Strategically, a Fed at its plateau against a BoJ with three scheduled decisions, plus the hedged-yield crossover that governs about $3.5tn of Japanese foreign holdings, gives −0.4083. The headline is tactically Bullish at conviction 2: target 159.40 into the 2026-10-28 FOMC, stop on a daily close below 156.30, and be flat before the BoJ on 2026-10-30. Strategically it is Bearish at conviction 3: target 151.50 by end-March 2027, where the rising 200-week average (about 151.3 by then) meets a three-touch support zone. The preferred strategic entry is near 159.40, not spot. The caveat is that the tactical call is thin. A post-valuation Tokyo core CPI of 2.7% and a suspected MoF rate check near 158 are specific threats to it, and a six-month short pays 207–234 pips of carry, so the 6M forward at 155.53, not spot, is its real breakeven.

Valuation is the reason the strategic distribution leans toward yen strength, not a reason to act in the next four weeks. bilateral_carry_analysis.carry_assessment: Policy basis carry is +262.5bp to a long USD/JPY position (USD 3.875% midpoint as of 2026-09-28 against JPY 1.25% as of 2026-09-29, gated CBPOL series); a rolled futures position earns 296.5bp a year (CME 6J calendar spread observed 2026-09-30), which by covered interest parity is the differential plus roughly -34bp of cross-currency basis. Carry-to-vol is 0.298 on the 3M ATM implied of 8.801% using the policy differential, 0.337 on the futures premium, 0.286 on 1M implied and 0.276 on 60-day realised. This is the second-highest G10 carry but it sits on one of the largest vol denominators among the major funding pairs. The regime is paying but not working: USD/JPY fell about 1.5% in the month to late September while the 10-year spread widened about 39bp, and every JPY cross except CHF/JPY fell while paying to be held. Carry pays a long about 34.5 pips a month at 157.87, or about 39 pips on the futures roll, which is 0.28 of a single day's ATR: a normal day erases three to four weeks of accrual. A six-month short pays 207–234 pips, so carry does not rescue a wrong direction and consumes about half the strategic expected value from spot.

That decoupling is the reason a record carry level does not translate mechanically into a bullish tactical rates stance. The two dates that can reprice the differential inside the window are the 2026-10-28 FOMC, where a hold is modal after Williams said there is no need for urgency and October odds fell below a coin flip, and the 2026-10-30 BoJ meeting with Outlook Report, where only about a quarter to a third of a 25bp move is priced against a Summary of Opinions in which the median member is hawkish. Probability-weighted, the expected four-week change in the differential is flat to slightly narrower, which offsets a carry level that pays a long position roughly 34 pips a month. Offsetting forces of similar size at the heaviest weight in the framework is what Neutral is for.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the first derivative of the differential, not its level, sets direction, and the derivative points down for this pair. The Fed's September projections put the median funds rate at 4.1% for both end-2026 and end-2027, so the FOMC sees itself within one 25bp move of a plateau that then lasts a year; the gated calendar gives it two decisions in the window, 2026-10-28 and the 2026-12-09 SEP meeting. The BoJ has three decisions in the same window - 2026-10-30 and 2027-01-22, both carrying Outlook Reports, plus 2026-12-18 - and has already delivered 50bp in 2026 from 0.75% to 1.25%. One Fed hike against two BoJ hikes narrows the gap from 262.5bp to about 237.5bp; a Fed that stops where it is against two BoJ hikes narrows it to 212.5bp. The long end is already doing this work independently of the policy rate: the JGB 10y is up about 141bp over a year to 3.06%, has crossed above the Bund, and sits roughly 259bp above the Swiss 10y, so Japan has stopped being the world's lowest-yielding major sovereign and the funding-currency proposition that anchored this pair for two decades is being repriced. Against that, the level still pays a long position roughly 2.6-3.0% a year, which is why confidence is 64 rather than higher: the thesis has to earn its carry back.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Adjusted from the 0.18 / 0.10 default. Reduced to fund the Factor 1, 4 and 7 increases. Justified bilaterally: the growth and inflation gap between these two economies is the widest and most stable in the G10 and is therefore largely a standing condition rather than a marginal driver - both central banks have already reacted to it, so incremental data surprises move this pair less than the policy and positioning channels do.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The macro differential is the cleanest pair-positive input in the framework and it is wide on both halves of the mandate. Growth: US GDP 2.1% y/y with Q2 revised up to 2.2% annualised, payrolls +162,000 against a 55,000 consensus, ISM manufacturing 54.5 and GDPNow 3.7%, against Japanese GDP of 0.73% y/y, zero contribution from private consumption in Q2, capex -0.9%, August industrial production -1.7% m/m against a +1.4% forecast, household spending -3.6% y/y and a Tankan large-manufacturer reading of +24 that missed its +25 consensus. Inflation: US headline CPI 3.4% and core PCE 3.0% against Japanese headline 1.9% and BoJ core of 1.7%, now a seventh consecutive month below target and decelerating. The transmission is asymmetric and runs through the reaction functions: US data at these levels keep the December Fed hike priced and keep real yields bid, while Japanese core below target hands the two BoJ dissenters their argument and lets the market keep fading the October meeting. The release that matters most for the pair in the window is US September CPI on 2026-10-14, because a firm core print lifts the US front end two weeks before the 2026-10-28 FOMC; the Japanese prints inside the window are consumption and wage data that are more likely to confirm the weak demand side than to upset it.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices the US expansion as durable and the Japanese core deceleration as a reason to fade the BoJ, which is internally consistent with the pair's carry but leaves the 2026-10-14 US CPI as the live pair-positive catalyst; a hawkish core surprise is not in the price.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the gap persists in levels but converges in trajectory, which neutralises the factor. On the US side the Fed's own projections take headline PCE from 3.7% in 2026 to 2.3% in 2027 and core PCE from 3.4% to 2.5%, with core CPI already at 2.4% and the consumer under strain - saving rate 4.1%, Conference Board confidence 81.9, Michigan 48.1, GDPNow down from 5.1% to 3.7% in two weeks. On the Japanese side the measured core is falling for a mechanical reason that expires: government energy subsidies pushed electricity to -2.4% y/y while the producer price index runs at 7.6% and Brent is up 53.6% on the year, so the suppression has a roll-off date and a 5.7-point pipeline behind it, with Tankan three-year inflation expectations at 2.6% and a fourth consecutive Shunto above 5%. The convergence is therefore two-sided: US disinflation removes the Fed's reason to extend, and Japanese subsidy roll-off plus pass-through gives the BoJ its reason to continue. Against that, Japanese potential growth near 0.5-1% and negative real wages mean the demand side deteriorates on the same clock the supply side firms on. Neutral at 55 is the honest reading of a differential that stays wide in level but stops widening.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: This is a haven-versus-haven pair, which is why its risk beta is unstable and currently uninformative. The level of risk appetite is benign: VIX 16.07-16.39, around the 34th-40th percentile of its post-2010 distribution, with the S&P 500 at the 88th percentile of its one-year range. The margin is deteriorating only in low-quality credit: US high-yield OAS widened 42-59bp over the month to 302-324bp, the 98th percentile of one year, while investment grade held at 83-86bp. For the pair, the two legs capture opposite halves of that signal - the dollar benefits from the real-yield and right-side-of-the-smile channel, the yen from the carry-unwind and repatriation channel - and at VIX 16 neither is activated. The evidence that the yen's September outperformance of every G10 currency happened with equities firm and VIX at 16 says that move was policy and positioning, not fear, so the haven channel is unspent rather than exhausted. Over four weeks a benign tape removes a tailwind the yen was not using and leaves the dollar's rate channel to do the work, which is mildly pair-positive; a credit-led spike would deliver an outsized pair-negative move precisely because the channel is unspent. Those cancel at this horizon.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the risk factor becomes an asymmetry argument and the asymmetry favours the yen leg, which makes it pair-negative. Investment-grade spreads at 83-86bp sit near the floor of their post-crisis range and the VIX at 16 is around the 37th percentile of five years, so the distribution of six-month changes is heavily skewed to widening, and high yield has already started at +42-59bp on the month. In a widening, the yen is the higher-beta beneficiary of the two legs through two channels the dollar does not have: repatriation of roughly 3.5 trillion dollars of Japanese holdings of foreign securities, and the unwind of positions short yen to fund higher-yielding assets - of which this pair, at 262.5bp, is the single largest funding expression. The counter-case is specific and real: if the widening becomes a dollar funding event rather than an equity or credit event, the dollar moves to the left side of the smile and the pair rises instead, which is the configuration the USD dossier flags at HY above 450bp with the JPY basis beyond -60bp. Confidence is held at 52 because the direction requires a shock that is not dated, and because the dollar's left-tail is a genuine offset rather than a rhetorical one.

The transition requires a shock rather than a date, which is why strategic confidence stays at 52.

The dollar leg is the opposite: the IMM aggregate dollar long rebuilt by 12.5bn dollars to 18.4bn in the week to 2026-09-22, the fastest weekly build in seven years, but the combined leveraged-plus-asset-manager measure sits only at the 44th percentile of its 25 cached weeks. Long yen against a mid-range dollar long means the crowded side of THIS pair is the short, and the pair's own option skew agrees: the payload's 25-delta risk reversal is -2.431 vol at one month, yen calls bid, the richest downside hedging demand in the G10. Composition moderates the severity rather than the direction - leveraged funds hold only +7,423 contracts and are effectively flat, so the remaining yen long is real money at +41,629 that liquidates over weeks rather than gapping. The pain trade over four weeks is a higher pair.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months speculative positioning mean-reverts out of the picture and institutional flow takes over, and on that measure both legs lean against the pair. On the yen side, long-dated JGBs now out-yield currency-hedged US Treasuries once 3-4% annual hedge costs are applied, with the JGB 10y at 3.06% and the 30y at 4.15%, which reverses the two-decade outflow from life insurers running 50-60% hedge ratios against about 3.5 trillion dollars of foreign securities; the 2027-03-31 Japanese fiscal year-end sits inside the window and adds its documented repatriation impulse on top. On the dollar side, the COFER reserve share fell to 56.70% in 2026-Q2 from 57.18% while the euro share rose, private foreigners sold 3.7bn dollars of US long-term securities in July with the adjusted long-term total at -27.9bn, and foreign official holdings of US Treasuries fell to a thirty-year low of 13%. Both flows are slow and both sell this pair. The honest caveat, which caps confidence at 55, is that the weekly Japanese securities data do not yet confirm a linear trend - foreign bond buying was +1,082.9bn yen in the week to 2026-09-16 after +111.9bn and -824.0bn - so this is a live arithmetic with noisy evidence rather than a confirmed flow.

A +72.0K speculative yen long at the 88th percentile is a four-week liability and nothing more, and it normalises historically within four to eight weeks of an extreme - late October or November, conveniently close to the 2026-10-30 Outlook Report. A hike on 2026-10-30 against a quarter-to-a-third-priced curve would therefore squeeze the street rather than the specs, and that is the single event most likely to make this factor wrong.

If hedge costs rise once more on a December Fed hike before they plateau, the crossover un-crosses and the single largest strategic flow in the thesis stops operating - and the pair's 262.5bp carry is then collecting against a short with no flow behind it.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: On levels the external comparison favours the yen and on marginal flow it favours the dollar, and over four weeks only the flow settles. Japan runs a current-account surplus of 5.03% of GDP against a US deficit of 3.0%, and the net international investment positions are +3.3 trillion dollars against -22.42 trillion - a comparison that would argue for a lower pair if it were FX-generative. It largely is not: July's Japanese surplus of 2,988.9bn yen rested on a primary income balance of 4,289.6bn yen that is overwhelmingly reinvested abroad, while the goods balance, which is settled, ran a fourth consecutive monthly deficit at 1,105.6bn yen in August with crude oil imports up 58.7% and total mineral fuels up 38.4%. Bilaterally, IMF DOTS 2024 goods flows show Japan with a 68.5bn dollar surplus against the United States - US exports to Japan 79.7bn against imports of 148.2bn - which is a structural yen-positive linkage, but it is invoiced and hedged predominantly in dollars and is dwarfed in monthly flow terms by Japan's Middle East energy bill. The terms-of-trade netting is unambiguous and pair-positive: the US is a net energy exporter with WTI up 49.6% on the year, Japan imports about 99% of its oil and sources 94.2% of its crude from the region at war. The next test is the 2026-10-07 Japanese current-account release.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At the strategic horizon the two legs' external negatives are close to the same size and point in opposite directions for the pair, which is a genuine Neutral rather than an evasion. Against the dollar: a current-account deficit that has widened for two quarters to 3.0% of GDP alongside a federal deficit near 6%, a NIIP of -22.42 trillion dollars whose income cost rises with every tick in US yields, financing that has shifted toward official and short-dated money, and a reserve share that fell 0.48pp in a quarter. Against the yen: a terms-of-trade transfer that is structural in origin and has not reversed, with four consecutive goods deficits, crude imports up 58.7%, LNG spot having risen more than 140% after the Ras Laffan strike, and both Korea and Taiwan out-exporting Japan in H1 2026 for the first time. The sign of the net depends almost entirely on Brent: a settlement that pulls crude toward 85 dollars removes Japan's transfer and the US gain simultaneously and makes the factor pair-negative, while a re-escalation makes it pair-positive. With the USD dossier putting a settlement at 25% over six months and escalation at 20%, that is a two-sided distribution around a factor whose level comparison favours the yen and whose flow comparison favours the dollar. Neutral at 55.

net_commodity_exposure.base_commodity_profile: USD: net energy exporter. WTI 96.16 dollars (+49.6% y/y), Henry Hub 3.18 dollars. Framework direction rule gives oil up a mild-to-moderate positive for the dollar via terms of trade and the energy component of the trade balance; the US also gains fiscally and in export receipts from elevated LNG and crude.
net_commodity_exposure.quote_commodity_profile: JPY: among the most energy-import-dependent currencies in the G10. Japan imports about 99% of its oil and sources 94.2% of its crude from the Middle East, and is a major LNG importer. Framework direction rules give oil up a strong negative for the yen and LNG (JKM) up a double-negative.
net_commodity_exposure.net_effect_calculation: Apply the framework rules leg by leg. Oil up: USD gets a mild-to-moderate positive (+), JPY gets a strong negative (--). Because the pair rises when USD strengthens against JPY, a (+) base and a (--) quote compound rather than offset, so oil up is clearly BULLISH USD/JPY. LNG up: USD mildly positive as an exporter, JPY double-negative as the world's largest LNG importer - again bullish for the pair. Gold up: mildly negative for the dollar on the -0.53 sixty-day DXY correlation and broadly neutral for the yen, a small pair-negative. Netting across the complex, the energy channel dominates by an order of magnitude and runs one way: USD/JPY is one of the most positively energy-levered pairs in the G10, which is precisely why four consecutive Japanese goods deficits with crude imports up 58.7% coexist with a US current account that is widening for reasons unrelated to energy.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_up_10pct: Bullish USD/JPY. Japan's monthly mineral-fuel bill rises roughly in proportion on a base of 2,464bn yen, widening the goods deficit that is actually settled in spot, while US terms of trade improve and the headline-inflation impulse keeps the Fed's December hike live. Both legs push the pair up; the only offset is a possible haven bid for the yen if the move comes from a Hormuz closure rather than demand.
net_commodity_exposure.scenario_oil_down_10pct: Bearish USD/JPY, and more cleanly than the up-case is bullish. Japan's deficit narrows and its real income transfer stops, while the US loses its terms-of-trade offset and headline inflation falls, reducing the Fed's reason to extend. A Gulf settlement is the specific path, which the USD dossier puts at 25% over six months.
net_commodity_exposure.dominant_commodity_driver: Brent crude, with JKM LNG as the amplifier. At 98-103 dollars and +53.6% y/y it is the single largest non-policy variable in this pair, and it is the only commodity whose moves do not cancel across the two legs.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Guidance diverges in direction and the sequence of the two meetings amplifies it. The Fed's 2026-09-16 statement committed to delivering price stability and was approved 12-0, but the guidance content is a plateau: 12 of 18 dots show one more 25bp move and the median is 4.1% for both 2026 and 2027, which the market has essentially bought - the gap between the implied path and the median dot is within about 5bp. The BoJ's guidance points the other way and is not bought: the 2026-09-18 statement guided continued rate increases, the Summary of Opinions released 2026-09-30 shows a majority favouring further hikes with one member arguing to accelerate, and yet only 25-38% of a hike is priced for 2026-10-30. The bilateral mechanism is that the pair reprices on the gap between guidance and pricing, and that gap is roughly 15-25bp on the quote leg against roughly nothing on the base leg. Sequencing matters: the gated calendar puts the FOMC on 2026-10-28 without projections and the BoJ on 2026-10-30 WITH an Outlook Report, so the quote-currency central bank speaks last and speaks with a projection round - the configuration that moves a pair hardest. A hawkish Outlook Report revision is the single most asymmetric communication event in the window.

tactical.what_is_priced: The market prices a Fed that follows its own dots and a BoJ that is a reluctant hiker constrained by politics; the first is fairly priced and the second is not, so the communication asymmetry inside the window sits on the quote leg and points the pair lower.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the guidance comparison is between an institution telling the market it is finished and one telling the market it is not. The Fed's projections show 4.1% at end-2027 and 3.9% at end-2028, which is explicit guidance toward a plateau, and its credibility - breakevens anchored at 2.36% with headline PCE at 3.4%, a 12-0 vote against public political pressure, and the Trump v. Cook ruling insulating governors - means that guidance is believed, which is exactly why it cannot generate further pair upside. The BoJ, by contrast, has two Outlook Reports inside the window on 2026-10-30 and 2027-01-22 plus a decision on 2026-12-18, and each is a scheduled vehicle for an upward forecast revision; it has also now delivered two hikes in 2026 under an administration widely assumed to prefer accommodation, which is the best available evidence on its independence. The second and underappreciated element is joint guidance on the exchange rate: after the late-July 2026 operation was confirmed by both the Japanese Ministry of Finance and the US Treasury, the market is dealing with a two-government statement of intent rather than a unilateral threat - and because the base-currency authority co-signed it, it is bilateral guidance that applies specifically to this pair. The offset is the Takaichi administration's expansionary fiscal programme and the political pressure it implies, which is why confidence is 62 rather than higher.

factors.horizon_split: Both horizons are Bearish for the pair and confidence rises strategically because the mechanism changes from one event to a cadence: tactically everything depends on a single Outlook Report the market prices at a quarter to a third, while strategically three BoJ decisions and a Fed SEP that confirms the plateau convert a binary into a sequence, raising the probability that at least one delivers the divergence the guidance already describes.

factors.weight_adjustment_reason: Adjusted from the 0.05 / 0.05 default. This pair carries a genuinely bilateral policy event that no other G10 pair has: a coordinated US-Japan intervention, executed in late July 2026 and confirmed by both treasuries, which truncates one tail of THIS pair specifically. A pair-specific official put is exactly the circumstance for raising event-risk weight; +0.02 at both horizons.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: The defining event-risk fact is bilateral by construction: in late July 2026 Japan and the United States conducted their first coordinated FX intervention since 2011, Japan selling roughly 8.45 trillion yen (52.8-59bn dollars, BoJ data suggesting about 58.97bn) with the US Treasury contributing an estimated maximum of 26.3bn, an operation that carried the pair from roughly 164 to 155.20. Finance Minister Katayama has said Japan will not hesitate to repeat it and Secretary Bessent confirmed the action countered disorderly moves. Because the base-currency authority co-signed, this is not a threat the market can test cheaply, and its practical four-week effect is a truncated upside tail for the pair with nothing symmetrical below. Dated risk inside the window clusters tightly: US September CPI on 2026-10-14, the FOMC on 2026-10-28 and the BoJ Outlook Report on 2026-10-30, two days apart - a configuration that produces discontinuous rather than diffusive price action. The Gulf is the two-sided element and it is unusually clean in this pair: escalation is pair-positive because it helps US terms of trade and hits Japan's import bill, settlement is pair-negative for the same reason inverted. Netting the truncated upside against a tactical positioning tailwind leaves this factor modestly pair-negative.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: Over one to six months the event calendar skews against the pair on both legs, which is unusual. On the base leg: the 2026-11-03 US midterms determine control of Congress, and the continuing resolution signed 2026-09-01 funds the government only to 2026-12-11, so a lame-duck Congress must act in the middle of the year-end funding turn - Fitch flagged gridlock and shutdown risk when affirming AA+ on 2026-08-13, and both outcomes are dollar-negative and route haven flows toward the yen, which is the pair's own quote currency. On the quote leg the main strategic risk runs the other way: the FY2027 budget compiled in December under an expansionary administration, with Fitch publicly committed to scrutinising it, is a yen-negative and pair-positive risk, and the 30y JGB at 4.15% shows the long end already disciplining fiscal signals. The Gulf remains two-sided but a settlement is likelier over six months than four weeks (25% on the USD dossier's odds), and settlement is pair-negative through both legs at once. Finally, a second coordinated operation becomes live if the pair revisits its pre-intervention highs, at roughly 20% conditional probability. Three of the four main strategic events are pair-negative, which is worth a Bearish stance at modest confidence.

The offsetting quote-leg risk, Japan's December budget, is also strategic, which is why the confidence gain is one point rather than several.

tactical.bilateral_analysis: Both sovereigns are deteriorating and neither has a dated trigger inside four weeks, so the differential is not actionable. The US carries debt held by the public at 101% of GDP, a FY2026 deficit of about 1.9-2.0 trillion dollars (5.8% of GDP) and net interest above 1 trillion dollars (3.3% of GDP, now above defence), with ratings stable one notch below AAA at all three agencies and September auctions clearing at successively higher yields. Japan carries roughly 260% of GDP, the heaviest in the developed world, but about 90% domestically held and with ratings stable at A1/A+/A, and its auctions are clearing well - the late-September 40-year drew the strongest demand since 2020 and the 2026-09-30 two-year cleared at 1.964%. The bilateral ranking is three to four notches in the dollar's favour on rating and heavily in the yen's favour on ownership structure. The pair-relevant transmission over four weeks is that higher yields on either side currently attract rather than repel capital: US July TIC inflows were 83.7bn dollars, and JGB yields actually FELL 2.5-4bp across the curve on 2026-09-30 on a report of fiscal reassurance from the Prime Minister. Two deteriorating sovereigns with clearing auctions and no scheduled event net to zero.

strategic.bilateral_analysis: At the strategic horizon each leg acquires a dated fiscal event and the two land within days of each other, pointing in opposite directions for the pair. On the dollar side the continuing resolution expires 2026-12-11, in the middle of the year-end funding turn, after midterms that determine whether a lame-duck Congress can act; Fitch has already named gridlock and shutdown risk, and net interest above 3.3% of GDP leaves no counter-cyclical space at full employment. On the yen side the FY2027 budget is compiled in the same December window under an administration pursuing expansion including a food tax cut, with Fitch publicly committed to reviewing the growth-versus-discipline balance and the 30y JGB already at 4.15% - and the transmission there is perverse for the yen, because rising JGB yields are yen-positive when driven by normalisation and yen-negative when driven by term premium, as the 222bp 2s30s suggests they increasingly are. One leg's fiscal risk is pair-negative and the other's is pair-positive, with similar timing and similar magnitude, so the honest net is Neutral. Confidence 54 reflects that both sets of ratings are stable and both bond markets are clearing.

strategic.path_expectation: The strategic path is a three-step decline that starts higher than spot. First, the tactical leg toward 159.40 into late October offers the preferred entry. The 2026-10-30 Outlook Report then starts the first leg down through the six-touch 156.52–157.98 band toward the 155.1–155.3 official-action floor in November. That floor is the first real test: a weekly close below 155.08 confirms the move. The December window — SEP on 2026-12-09, CR expiry on 2026-12-11, BoJ on 2026-12-18, plus year-end basis widening — is the likely pause. A retracement to 156.5–157.5 should hold below the 158.51 200-day. The third leg runs from the 2027-01-22 Outlook Report into the 2027-03-31 fiscal year-end. Below 155 the structure is thin down to 151.60, so this leg can be faster, and it ends where the rising 200-week (about 151.3) meets the three-touch zone. Volatility should run near or above the 8.75% six-month implied, with intervention-style gaps rather than drift. Entry, stop and sizing (strategic): Preferred entry - sell 159.00–159.40 after the tactical leg; the fallback is selling a weekly close below 156.52 on a confirmed break. Stop - weekly close above 162.60, i.e. 320 pips (2.0%) from 159.40, about 2.6 daily ATRs. Targets - 155.30 first, 151.50 final. Sizing - at conviction 3, use one full standard risk unit (a 0.50% risk at a 2.0% stop implies a notional of about 0.25× capital). Alternative instrument - 3–6M USD/JPY puts, bought after 2026-10-30, avoid the 207–234 pips of six-month carry a forward short pays.

consensus_divergence.why_we_differ: Three bilateral factors are weighted differently. First, Flows and Positioning: consensus models this pair off the rate differential and the risk regime and treats the September CFTC flip as noise, where we treat a 212.6K-contract swing through the +80K historical extreme, a 30% collapse in open interest and a -2.431 vol one-month risk reversal as a four-week liability that has to clear before the strategic view can be expressed. Second, USD Liquidity: consensus assigns almost no weight to the hedged-yield crossover that governs Japanese institutional allocation, where we make it a pair-negative strategic factor at a 0.12 weight. Third, Event Risk: consensus treats the late-July intervention as a Japanese policy nuisance, where we treat a joint operation co-signed by the US Treasury as bilateral guidance on this specific pair that truncates the upside tail and nothing below it. Netting those, we are more bearish than consensus on mechanism and less bearish on extent. Research addendum: fresh research does not support the carried consensus figures; the aggregator now shows 158.36 at one month, 158.34 by December 2026, 156.94 by March 2027 and 155.00 by June 2027, so the JPY dossier's verification correction appears to have gone the wrong way. The tactical call is therefore not contrarian, and the strategic view is more aggressive than consensus on both timing and level.
consensus_divergence.payoff_if_right: The tactical call is a sequencing edge rather than a directional one, and is consensus-adjacent on current figures, so its payoff-if-right is smaller than the scored text implied. Strategically, being right on direction while less extended than the older 145.40 path means the view survives a December pause. If consensus is right at six months (around 155–157), a short from spot earns roughly 100–300 pips gross and close to nothing after carry, which is a further reason the strategic entry should be near 159.40, not at spot.
consensus_divergence.risk_if_wrong: Two asymmetric ways to be wrong. If consensus is right on timing, the pair falls immediately and the tactical Bullish call is wrong from day one - the most likely trigger is a hawkish Outlook Report on 2026-10-30 against a 25-38% priced curve, which would squeeze a street that is short yen at -108,284 dealer contracts. If consensus is right on magnitude, the strategic call under-earns without losing money. The genuine loss case for the strategic view is a BoJ that stalls at 1.25% through 2027-01-22 while the Bed delivers on 2026-12-09, which restores the carry logic and leaves a short paying 262.5bp a year into a widening differential.

cross_horizon_consistency.explanation: A 0.535-point divergence, and it is mechanical rather than a hedge. Three factors flip sign between horizons and each flips for a stated reason. Policy and Rates is Neutral tactically because the differential's level is static and demonstrably not transmitting, and Bearish strategically because the Fed is at its plateau while the BoJ has three scheduled decisions, two with Outlook Reports. Flows and Positioning is Bullish tactically on a crowded real-money yen long at the 88th percentile, and Bearish strategically on the hedged-yield crossover and a falling dollar reserve share - different flows on different clocks. USD Liquidity is Neutral tactically because dollars are abundant and expensive with no stress, and Bearish strategically because that same high price of dollars is the hedge cost whose plateau releases Japanese institutional money homeward. Inflation and Growth moves from Bullish to Neutral as the US disinflates and the Japanese energy subsidy rolls off.
cross_horizon_consistency.inflection_point: The 2026-10-28 FOMC and the 2026-10-30 BoJ meeting with Outlook Report, two days apart, with the BoJ second. That 48-hour cluster is simultaneously the point at which the speculative yen long is resolved and the first scheduled opportunity for the quote-currency central bank to revise its forecast path upward. A secondary inflection is the normalisation of CFTC positioning below about +30K contracts, historically four to eight weeks after an extreme, which places it in late October or November.
cross_horizon_consistency.trading_implication: Sequence, do not net. The two views are compatible if the tactical positioning liability is allowed to clear first: the tactical view has to be established before the 2026-10-28 to 2026-10-30 cluster, and the strategic view after it, when the event premium has decayed and the vol surface is cheapest at the back end (8.751% at 190.6 days against 9.183% at 36.7). Netting them into a single flat position discards the only edge either one has, which is timing. Implementation in levels: (1) run the tactical long from 157.48 (scaled average) toward 159.40, with the 156.30 close-stop; (2) exit by the 2026-10-29 close; (3) establish the strategic short (or 3–6M puts) at 159.00–159.40 if the tactical target prints, or on a weekly close below 156.52 if it does not; (4) use the weekly-close stop above 162.60. The tactical long and the strategic short should never be held at the same time; the hand-over happens in a single session before the BoJ.

catalysts.rationale: The first major print after the valuation date and the determinant of whether the Fed's one-more-hike path survives to 2026-12-09. A strong print re-widens a front-end spread already near +299bp and is pair-positive; a soft print compresses it and hands the strategic thesis an early confirmation. August printed +162,000 against a 55,000 consensus, so the bar has been reset high.

Broker commentary reports that Tokyo core inflation accelerated to 2.7%, exceeding the Bank of Japan's 2% target for the first time in nine months. If confirmed, this is the first observable sign of the subsidy roll-off and pass-through that the strategic case relies on. It also directly threatens the tactical premise that the October BoJ is under-priced only at the margin. This is single-source and unverified here; it is treated as a signpost, not a re-score.

The address sets out the expansionary fiscal programme and a pledge to respond to market moves. Fiscal expansion under an administration seen to prefer accommodation is the standing yen-negative in the political file, and is pair-positive at the margin.

catalysts.event: FOMC minutes of the 15-16 September meeting
catalysts.rationale: The minutes reveal how many participants argued for a faster pace behind a 12-0 vote in which 12 of 18 dots showed another move. A broad hawkish majority lifts December odds and the US front end, widening the differential against a BoJ the market is simultaneously fading - a pair-positive combination that works through the base leg alone.

catalysts.event: Japan August current account and trade detail
catalysts.rationale: Tests whether the primary income surplus of 4,289.6bn yen continues to outrun a goods deficit that has run four consecutive months at 1,105.6bn with crude imports up 58.7%. The composition is the pair-relevant part: income is reinvested abroad and does not convert, while the goods deficit settles in spot and sells yen every month.

August was 3.4% headline and 2.4% core with gasoline a third of the monthly rise. A core print at or above 0.3% m/m sustains US real yields two weeks before the FOMC and is pair-positive; 0.1% or below knocks the December hike toward a coin flip and removes the tactical case. Japan has no comparable release inside the same fortnight, so the asymmetry sits on the base leg.

catalysts.event: US September retail sales and PPI
catalysts.rationale: August retail sales rose 1.2% with the control group at 1.4% and real PCE at 0.6% m/m. Another strong print sustains a 1.4pp growth gap over Japan, whose own August industrial production fell 1.7% m/m and household spending 3.6% y/y - the growth-differential channel that carries Factor 2's tactical weight in this pair.

catalysts.event: US Treasury International Capital data for August
catalysts.rationale: July showed 83.7bn dollars of headline inflows but private long-term selling of 3.7bn and an adjusted long-term total of -27.9bn. A second month of private selling of US duration is direct evidence for the strategic flow thesis, and because the marginal foreign seller of Treasuries at these hedge costs is Japanese, it reads simultaneously as repatriation into the quote currency.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC decision (no projections) — gated calendar
catalysts.rationale: A hold at 3.75-4.00% is modal after Williams said there is no need for urgency and October odds fell below a coin flip. A hawkish hold that keeps December live is mildly pair-positive; a hike is clearly pair-positive; a dovish hold two days before the BoJ's Outlook Report is the worst configuration for a long position because it stacks the base-leg disappointment immediately ahead of the quote-leg risk.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting with Outlook Report — gated calendar, projection round
catalysts.rationale: The single most asymmetric event for this pair in the window and the inflection between the two horizons. A quarterly forecast round at which the Bank can raise its CPI path, held against a Summary of Opinions in which a majority favour further hikes and one member urged acceleration, while only 25-38% of a 25bp move is priced. It falls two days after the FOMC, so the quote-currency bank speaks last and with projections - the configuration that moves a pair hardest. Current market pricing is lower still: MUFG notes the Japanese rate market went from pricing in around 10bps of hikes by the October policy meeting and that has now dropped to around 5bps.

Control of Congress determines whether a lame-duck session can fund the government past 2026-12-11. A divided outcome raises shutdown risk and revives the governance debate Fitch named when affirming AA+, and in this pair the haven flow from US political risk runs directly into the quote currency rather than into a third leg.

catalysts.event: Federal Reserve FOMC decision with Summary of Economic Projections — gated calendar, SEP
catalysts.rationale: The meeting at which the Fed either confirms a plateau near 4.00-4.25% or extends the path into 2027. A delivered hike with an unchanged 2027 dot marks the cycle top and is the pivot the strategic bearish case needs; a 2027 dot revised up to 4.4% would widen the differential against a BoJ moving 25bp at a time and invalidate it.

catalysts.event: Expiry of the continuing resolution (US government funding deadline)
catalysts.rationale: The CR signed 2026-09-01 funds agencies only to this date, so a shutdown would land in the middle of the year-end funding turn. The bilateral complication is that the same event widens the cross-currency basis seasonally, which is pair-positive, so the net depends on whether governance risk or dollar funding demand dominates - the clearest two-sided date in the strategic window.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting — gated calendar
catalysts.rationale: The second scheduled BoJ opportunity in the window, priced near 39%. If October delivers a hold with a hawkish forecast revision, this becomes the market's focal point and pricing should converge upward; a second consecutive hold with no revision is the date on which the strategic compression mechanism starts to fail.

catalysts.event: Bank of Japan Monetary Policy Meeting with Outlook Report — gated calendar, projection round
catalysts.rationale: The second Outlook Report inside the strategic window and the point by which two of three scheduled hike opportunities will have passed, so it is where a stalled normalisation becomes visible and where a delivered second hike would take the differential to about 212.5bp if the Fed has stopped. It sits just beyond a strict three-month horizon and is noted as such.

This is the yen's best-documented seasonal. Corporate and institutional repatriation concentrates in late February and March. This year it coincides with the hedged-yield crossover, so the seasonal and structural flows reinforce each other. It is the final impulse in the strategic path toward 151.50.
